meanings.usage: 通常修饰工作、劳动等需要体力完成的活动
用于描述从事非体力办公室工作的人群或相关属性
常用搭配sacrifice sth for sth，表为了某物舍弃另一物
可指社会地位带来的特殊优待，也可表荣幸做某事
除表好奇的，还可修饰事物表示不寻常、值得注意的
英式英语表述，对应美式英语garbage man
用来描述人因处境尴尬、害羞的状态，修饰事物用embarrassing
常用复数形式，指工作时穿的防护性服装
放在名词前，指和自己有相同身份、处境的人
指个人在社会、组织中的层级地位，不可数名词

phrases.usage: 将某人称作、把某人称为，用来表达对某人的称谓

examples.en: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as 'white-collar workers'.
examples.zh: 在办公室工作的人常常被称作“白领工人”。

examples.en: He is often referred to as the best basketball player of his generation.
examples.zh: 他常被称为他那一代人中最好的篮球运动员。

phrases.usage: 引起；导致；使发生，后接表示结果类的名词

examples.en: This can give rise to curious situations.
examples.zh: 这就可能引起一些奇怪的现象。

examples.en: Poor communication may give rise to misunderstandings between team members.
examples.zh: 沟通不畅可能会导致团队成员之间产生误会。

phrases.usage: 就……而言；在……的情况下，用来引出具体的例子或情况

examples.en: As it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman.
examples.zh: 在阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯的情况中就是如此，他是埃尔斯米尔公司的清洁工。

examples.en: The new policy is quite flexible, especially in the case of small businesses.
examples.zh: 这项新政策很灵活，对小企业来说尤其如此。

phrases.usage: 太……而不能……，用来表达否定含义，说明程度过高导致无法做某事

examples.en: Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
examples.zh: 阿尔弗太尴尬了，以至于没法和妻子说自己工作的事。

examples.en: The little boy was too short to reach the book on the top shelf.
examples.zh: 这个小男孩太矮了，够不到顶层架子上的书。

phrases.usage: 非常值得……，后面接名词或动名词，表付出的代价是值得的

examples.en: He feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
examples.zh: 他觉得地位提升了，损失这点钱是非常值得的。

examples.en: The view from the mountain top is well worth the two-hour climb.
examples.zh: 爬两个小时的山来看山顶的景色是非常值得的。

grammar.title: 定语从句 (Attributive Clause)
grammar.structure: 先行词 + 关系代词/关系副词 + 从句剩余部分
grammar.definition: 在复合句中修饰名词或代词的从句，用来对先行词进行修饰限定 用来补充说明先行词的特征、属性等，常用关系代词who指代人，which指代物，that既可指人或物

examples.en: People who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
examples.zh: 从事体力劳动的人通常比坐办公室的人收入高得多。

examples.en: The book that you lent me last week is very interesting.
examples.zh: 你上周借给我的那本书非常有意思。

grammar.title: 将来进行时 (Future Continuous Tense)
grammar.structure: will be + 动词的现在分词（doing）
grammar.definition: 表示将来某个时间正在进行的动作，或者将来某段时间内持续进行的动作 用来表达对将来动作的客观描述，比一般将来时更强调动作在未来的持续性、进行状态

examples.en: He will soon be working in an office.
examples.zh: 他不久就要在办公室工作了。

examples.en: This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Paris.
examples.zh: 明天这个时候，我正飞往巴黎。

grammar.title: such引导的倒装句
grammar.structure: Such + be + 主语 + that引导的结果状语从句
grammar.definition: 为了强调表语部分，将such置于句首，句子需要部分倒装，用来加强语气 用来突出强调某事物的性质、特点，后接that从句说明该特点带来的结果

examples.en: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
examples.zh: 很多人常常愿意牺牲更高的薪水来换取成为白领的优待，这就是人之常情。

examples.en: Such is the power of music that it can make people forget their sadness.
examples.zh: 这就是音乐的力量，它能让人们忘记悲伤。

patterns.pattern: A receive far more money than B

original.en: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
original.zh: 如今，从事体力劳动的人通常比坐办公室的人收入高得多。

imitations.en: Nowadays, skilled technicians often receive far more money than ordinary office clerks.
imitations.zh: 如今，技术娴熟的技工通常比普通办公室职员收入高得多。

imitations.en: In many cities, people who work in the catering industry often receive far more money than new graduates.
imitations.zh: 在很多城市，从事餐饮行业的人通常比刚毕业的学生收入高得多。

patterns.pattern: A be willing to sacrifice A for the privilege of B

original.en: A great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
original.zh: 很多人常常愿意牺牲更高的薪水来换取成为白领的优待。

imitations.en: Many young people are willing to sacrifice their free time for the privilege of studying at a top university.
imitations.zh: 很多年轻人愿意牺牲自己的空闲时间来换取在顶尖大学学习的机会。

imitations.en: He was willing to sacrifice a stable job for the privilege of starting his own business.
imitations.zh: 他愿意牺牲一份稳定的工作来换取自己创业的机会。

patterns.pattern: A do this for + 时间段, and B keep the secret

original.en: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret.
original.zh: 阿尔弗这样做了两年多，他的清洁工同事们都替他保守秘密。

imitations.en: She hid her illness from her family for three months and her close friends kept her secret.
imitations.zh: 她向家人隐瞒了自己的病情三个月，她的密友们都替她保守秘密。

imitations.en: He prepared a surprise birthday party for his wife for a week and all their common friends kept the secret.
imitations.zh: 他为妻子准备惊喜生日派对准备了一周，他们的共同好友都替他保守秘密。

text.title: The double life of Alfred Bloggs

lines.en: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
lines.zh: 如今，从事体力劳动的人的收入一般要比坐办公室的人高出许多。

lines.en: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as "white-collar workers' for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
lines.zh: 坐办公室的之所以常常被称作“白领工人”，就是因为他们通常是穿着硬领白衬衫，系着领带去上班。

lines.en: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
lines.zh: 许多人常常情愿放弃较高的薪水以换取做白领工人的殊荣，此乃人之常情。

lines.en: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
lines.zh: 而这常常会引起种种奇怪的现象，在埃尔斯米尔公司当清洁工的艾尔弗雷德。布洛斯就是一个例子。艾尔弗结婚时，感到非常难为情，而没有将自己的职业告诉妻子。

lines.en: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.
lines.zh: 他只说在埃尔斯米尔公司上班。

lines.en: Every morning, he left home dressed in a smart black suit.
lines.zh: 每天早晨，他穿上一身漂亮的黑色西装离家上班，然后换上工作服，当8个小时清洁工。

lines.en: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
lines.zh: 晚上回家前，他洗个淋浴，重新换上那身黑色西服。
两年多以来，艾尔弗一直这样，他的同事也为他保守秘密。

lines.en: He took a shower and changed back into his suit.
lines.zh: 艾尔弗的妻子一直不知道她嫁给了一个清洁工，而且她永远也不会知道了，因为艾尔弗已找到薪职，不久就要坐办公室里工作了。

lines.en: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret Alf's wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job.
lines.zh: 他将来挣的钱只有他现在的一半。

lines.en: He will soon be working in an office.
lines.zh: 不过他觉得，地位升高了，损失点儿钱也值得。

lines.en: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
lines.zh: 从此，艾尔弗可以一天到晚穿西服了。

lines.en: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him 'Mr.. Bloggs', not 'Alf'.
lines.zh: 别人将称呼他为“布洛格斯先生”，而不再叫他“艾尔弗”了。

questions.q: Why did Alf want a white-collar job?
questions.zh: 阿尔弗雷德为什么想要一份白领工作？
questions.a: Because he was willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming a white-collar worker; he felt that his rise in status was well worth the loss of money.
questions.aZh: 因为他情愿放弃更高的薪水，以换取做白领工人的殊荣；他觉得地位提升了，损失点钱也值得。
questions.hint: 答案出自第3段 willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers 与末段 his rise in status is well worth the loss of money。

questions.q: What did Alf tell his wife about his job?
questions.zh: 阿尔弗雷德对妻子是怎么说他的工作的？
questions.a: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation; he never mentioned that he was a dustman.
questions.aZh: 他只告诉妻子自己在埃尔斯米尔公司上班，从未提起自己是清洁工。
questions.hint: 见第5段 He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.

questions.q: How did Alf keep his job a secret every day?
questions.zh: 阿尔弗雷德每天怎样隐瞒自己的工作？
questions.a: Every morning he left home dressed in a smart black suit, then changed into overalls to spend eight hours as a dustman; before returning home he took a shower and changed back into his suit.
questions.aZh: 每天早晨他穿着漂亮的黑色西装离家，然后换上工作服当八小时清洁工；晚上回家前先洗个淋浴，再换回西服。
questions.hint: 见第6至8段关于他每天换装的描写。

questions.q: Who kept his secret, and how long did his double life last?
questions.zh: 谁替他保守秘密？他的双重生活持续了多久？
questions.a: His fellow dustmen kept his secret, and he did this for over two years.
questions.aZh: 他的清洁工同事们为他保密，这样的双重生活持续了两年多。
questions.hint: 见第9段 his fellow dustmen kept his secret... did this for over two years。

questions.q: What does the title 'the double life' suggest, and why is the ending ironic?
questions.zh: “双重生活”这一标题暗示了什么？为什么结局带有讽刺意味？
questions.a: It suggests that Alf lived two identities — a smartly dressed office man outside and a dustman at work. The ending is ironic because the only way he can stop lying is to become what he pretended to be: he must give up half his pay just to be called 'Mr. Bloggs'.
questions.aZh: 它暗示阿尔弗雷德过着两种身份——外表是西装革履的上班族，实际却是清洁工。结局的讽刺在于：他终止谎言的办法竟是变成自己假装的那种人——为了被称作“布洛格斯先生”，他不得不放弃一半收入。
questions.hint: 综合标题与末段 He will be earning only half as much... his rise in status is well worth the loss of money... others will call him 'Mr. Bloggs'。

translation:
如今，从事体力劳动的人的收入一般要比坐办公室的人高出许多。
坐办公室的之所以常常被称作“白领工人”，就是因为他们通常是穿着硬领白衬衫，系着领带去上班。
许多人常常情愿放弃较高的薪水以换取做白领工人的殊荣，此乃人之常情。
而这常常会引起种种奇怪的现象，在埃尔斯米尔公司当清洁工的艾尔弗雷德。
布洛斯就是一个例子。
艾尔弗结婚时，感到非常难为情，而没有将自己的职业告诉妻子。
他只说在埃尔斯米尔公司上班。
每天早晨，他穿上一身漂亮的黑色西装离家上班，然后换上工作服，当8个小时清洁工。
晚上回家前，他洗个淋浴，重新换上那身黑色西服。
两年多以来，艾尔弗一直这样，他的同事也为他保守秘密。
艾尔弗的妻子一直不知道她嫁给了一个清洁工，而且她永远也不会知道了，因为艾尔弗已找到薪职，不久就要坐办公室里工作了。
他将来挣的钱只有他现在的一半。
不过他觉得，地位升高了，损失点儿钱也值得。
从此，艾尔弗可以一天到晚穿西服了。
别人将称呼他为“布洛格斯先生”，而不再叫他“艾尔弗”了。
title: The Double Life of Alfred Bloggs
subtitle: 阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯的双重生活

lead.question: 阿尔弗雷德·布洛格斯本是清洁工，为何却一心想当白领、还向妻子隐瞒职业？
lead.warmup: 本课讲一个有趣的社会现象：体力劳动者收入更高，许多人却宁愿少挣钱也要当“白领”。清洁工艾尔弗雷德·布洛格斯就是这样一位“双重生活”者——他每天西装革履出门，再换上工作服扫街，连妻子都蒙在鼓里。阅读时请注意作者如何用对比和幽默揭示这种身份焦虑，并留意文中现在完成时的用法。
goals: 掌握 manual work, white-collar, collar, dustman, overalls, corporation, fellow, status 等职业与身份词汇。
理解并运用 too...to、half as much as、sacrifice A for B 等句型。
区分现在完成时与一般过去时，特别是与 ago / for 的搭配习惯。
读懂课文的社会讽刺意味，能用英语复述阿尔弗雷德的“双重生活”。
lead.summary: 课文指出，如今体力劳动者的收入常高于坐办公室的人，可许多人仍愿牺牲高薪去换取当“白领”的殊荣。清洁工艾尔弗雷德·布洛格斯就是如此：他为埃尔斯米尔公司扫街，却对妻子谎称在公司上班，每天西装出门、换上工作服干活，两年多来靠同事保密。如今他即将真正坐进办公室，收入减半，但他觉得地位提升值得。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：现在完成时不能与表示过去的具体时间状语（如 ago）连用——“Alf has worked as a dustman two years ago”是病句，应改为“Alf worked as a dustman two years ago”或“Alf has worked as a dustman for two years”。

exercises.q: 汉译英：如今，从事体力劳动的人往往比坐办公室的人挣得多得多。
exercises.a: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.

exercises.q: 填空：People who work in offices are frequently referred to as '___ workers' for the simple reason that they usually wear a ___ and tie to go to work.
汉译英：艾尔弗太难为情了，没把工作的事告诉妻子。
exercises.a: Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.

exercises.q: 填空：Alf worked as a ___ for the Ellesmere ___ , and after leaving home in a smart black suit he changed into ___ .
exercises.note: dustman 清洁工；overalls 工作服

exercises.q: 改错：Alf has worked as a dustman two years ago.
exercises.a: Alf worked as a dustman two years ago.（或：Alf has worked as a dustman for two years.）
exercises.note: ago 不与现在完成时连用

exercises.q: 改为被动语态：His fellow dustmen kept his secret.
exercises.a: His secret was kept by his fellow dustmen.
exercises.note: keep a secret 保守秘密

exercises.q: 汉译英：他挣的钱将只有过去的一半，但他觉得地位提升值得这点损失。
exercises.a: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
exercises.note: half as much as 一半之多

quiz.q: 阿尔弗雷德为什么想要一份白领工作？
options: Because he wanted to earn more money.
Because he wanted the privilege and higher status of being a white-collar worker.
Because he was tired of physical labour.
Because his wife wanted him to change jobs.

quiz.q: 阿尔弗雷德对妻子是怎么说自己的工作的？
options: He told her he was a dustman.
He told her he worked for the Corporation.
He told her he was out of work.
He told her he owned the Corporation.

quiz.q: 阿尔弗雷德每天是怎么伪装自己的？
options: He wore overalls to the office.
He left home in a smart black suit and changed into overalls at work.
He worked only at night.
He never went home after work.

quiz.q: 谁帮阿尔弗雷德保守了秘密？
options: His wife.
His boss.
His fellow dustmen.
His neighbours.

quiz.q: 换了新工作后，阿尔弗雷德的收入会怎样？
options: He will earn twice as much as before.
He will earn about the same as before.
He will earn only half as much as he used to.
He will earn nothing at all.

quiz.q: 下面哪一句正确使用了现在完成时？
options: Alf has worked as a dustman two years ago.
Alf has just found another job.
Alf is finding another job just now.
Alf finds another job recently.
quiz.note: 现在完成时不可与 ago 连用。
